newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny says delays May steel price hike.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny says delays May steel price hike.

text.p: The chairman of Allegheny Teledyne Inc said Thursday the company's five percent price hike on flat-rolled stainless steel, originally scheduled for May 6, was delayed until at least June 2.

"The May 6 increase has now been delayed until sometime after June 1," Richard Simmons, Allegheny Teledyne chairman, told reporters after the company's annual shareholders meeting. "The market will determine whether that increase goes in in June or July or August."

Simmons said imports are continuing to enter the domestic market at a high level, keeping downward pressure on pricing and dampening the chances for a successful price hike. He said steel demand is strong but prices are remaining sluggish due to the oversupply.
Stainless steel prices have fallen about 20 percent in the past year.
Simmons also told reporters his company may make an acquisition of "material size" by the end of the year.
"We will attempt to make a material strategic acquisition that will support one of the segments of the company and it would not be appropriate for me to identify which segment," he said.
